title: Establish enterprise triage gateway for Hosted API feature requests (chat/streaming/tool-calls/structured-output)
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an operational 'Enterprise Request Gateway' and prioritization rubric specifically for Hosted API feature requests from enterprise customers that touch chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. The goal is to reduce time-to-decision for R&D while ensuring security, SLA impact, and rollout feasibility are evaluated consistently.

Problem statement:
We continue to receive high-volume, high-complexity feature asks from enterprise customers that span multiple product domains (chat UX, streaming reliability, tool-calling semantics, and structured outputs formatting). Our current intake is inconsistent: some asks jump to engineering, others to design, and SLA/cost/compatibility trade-offs are surfaced late. This causes rework, missed expectations, and priority noise for Dedicated/Private sales motion.

Objectives:
- Standardize intake so every enterprise request is scored for: security surface, SLA/latency risk, implementation effort, cross-team dependencies, and potential revenue/SAM impact.
- Produce a one-page triage artifact per request with recommended path: Fast-track (can be done by Hosted API roadmap), Pilot (dedicated/partner), or Long-term (Private/Dedicated only).
- Reduce average decision latency from 14 days to 3 business days for enterprise asks that require non-trivial engineering effort.

Proposed prioritization rubric (fields scored 1-5):
- Customer ARR/Strategic importance
- SLA/latency sensitivity
- Data-sensitivity/compliance impact
- Engineering effort (est. points)
- UX/Design effort
- Risk of model/regression quality
- Revenue enablement (new customers/expansion)

Decision thresholds (example):
- Fast-track: score >=22 and engineering effort <=8 points
- Pilot: 15-21 and requires controlled rollout + feature flagging
- Long-term: <15 or requires infra/private deployment changes

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form available to Sales/CS that captures required fields and auto-populates initial rubric scores.
- Triage committee (PM + Eng lead + Security + Solutions Eng) meets twice weekly with a shared triage board in Linear.
- A template one-page decision doc is auto-created and stored (Confluence link) for each triaged request.
- Telemetry hooks: tag triaged requests so we can report decision latency and outcome distribution.

Examples of incoming asks (anonymized):
- Large fintech: low-latency streaming with guarantee for function-call order and audit logs. (SLA-sensitive, compliance)
- Healthcare partner: need structured JSON outputs with schema validation + on-prem option. (Compliance + Private tilt)
- Marketplace platform: tool-calling multi-step workflows with retry semantics and user token passthrough. (Security + integration complexity)

Decision log so far:
- 2026-02-22: Initial rubric draft reviewed by Solutions Eng (Aisha Kapoor) and Security (Ravi Patel). Security requested explicit KMS/HSM check for tool-calling and token passthrough.
- 2026-02-25: Engineering (Liam Chen) suggested adding an "implementation complexity" cap to avoid long-running infra projects being misclassified as Fast-track.
- 2026-03-02: Design (Maya Alvarez) provided a template for the one-page doc and asked that we include minimal mockups only for UX-impacting asks.

Open questions:
- Should the triage gateway automatically surface recommended model variants (quantized, batched-friendly) as part of engineering score?
- What SLA tiers do we expose publicly vs. in enterprise proposals?
- Should we allow Sales to request 'pre-approved pilot' for high-revenue accounts that short-circuits the 3-day rule?

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Build intake form prototype in Airtable/Formstack (Owner: Solutions Eng, due 2026-03-05).
- Implement triage board in Linear with a triage label and required fields (Owner: PM, due 2026-03-10).
- Security to provide checklist for token/KMS requirements for tool-calling flows (Owner: Security, due 2026-03-12).
- Engineering to propose a lightweight pre-check for model-variant compatibility (Owner: ENG runtime lead, due 2026-03-12).

Links/artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Enterprise+Hosted+Intake+Gateway (template page)
- Intake prototype (Airtable): https://airtable.com/shrExample123
- Design template PRD: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/example-design-template

Notes on rollout and measurement:
- We'll report daily triage counts and decision lag in the PM dashboard. Metrics: mean time to decision, % fast-track, pilot conversion to roadmap, broken down by customer segment.

If approved, this ticket will be used as the operating playbook and will spawn per-customer sub-issues for implementation work requiring engineering/design resource allocation.
